title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text: This post examines historical trends in human longevity and economic development from 1952 to 2007. Through data manipulation and visualization in R, we will track the global median life expectancy over time and compare regional outcomes.

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Dataset Overview
Data Source: The Gapminder dataset
License: Free to use under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
The dataset provides country-level records over 5-year intervals. The glimpse output below shows the structure of the data, including population, continent, and life expectancy.

library(gapminder)
library(dplyr)

glimpse(gapminder)

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Continental Overview in 2007
Grouping the 2007 data by continent to calculate median life expectancy and GDP per capita. Using medians reduces the impact of extreme outliers within each continent.

summary_2007 <- gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(
    median_life_exp = median(lifeExp),
    median_gdp = median(gdpPercap),
    total_population = sum(as.numeric(pop)),
    num_countries = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(median_life_exp))

knitr::kable(summary_2007, digits = 2, caption = "2007 Continental Summary")

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Longitudinal Life Expectancy Trajectory
Calculating and plotting the global median life expectancy across all available survey years to view the aggregate trend over time.

yearly_trend <- gapminder |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(median_life_exp = median(lifeExp))

plot(
  yearly_trend$year,
  yearly_trend$median_life_exp,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  col = "navy",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Median Life Expectancy (Years)",
  main = "Global Median Life Expectancy (1952 - 2007)"
)
grid()







Figure 1: Global median life expectancy progression from 1952 to 2007.






Visualizing Continental Life Expectancy (2007)
This bar chart provides a direct visual comparison of median life expectancy across the five continents using the 2007 subset.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(summary_2007, aes(x = continent, y = median_life_exp, fill = continent)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(
    title = "Median Life Expectancy by Continent (2007)",
    x = "Continent",
    y = "Median Life Expectancy (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")








Observations from 2007 Data:

Highest Life Expectancy: Oceania and Europe lead the dataset, with median life expectancies over 76 years.
Middle Range: The Americas and Asia group closely together in the low 70s.
Lowest Life Expectancy: Africa has the lowest median life expectancy at 52.9 years, creating a noticeable gap between it and the other four continents.

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (Python)
text:
Regional Summary (2007)
Aggregating the 2007 data by continent establishes a modern baseline. Using median values for life expectancy and GDP per capita minimizes the skew from extreme national outliers.

recent_summary = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"] == 2007]
    .groupby("continent")
    .agg(
        median_life_exp=("lifeExp", "median"),
        median_gdp=("gdpPercap", "median"),
        total_pop=("pop", "sum"),
        country_count=("country", "count")
    )
    .sort_values(by="median_life_exp", ascending=False)
    .reset_index()
)

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (Python)
text:
55-Year Progress (1952 vs 2007)
Comparing the earliest and latest available years highlights the absolute growth in global life expectancy during the post-WWII era.

comparison = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"].isin([1952, 2007])]
    .groupby(["continent", "year"])["lifeExp"]
    .mean()
    .unstack()
    .rename(columns={1952: "life_exp_1952", 2007: "life_exp_2007"})
)

comparison["gain_years"] = comparison["life_exp_2007"] - comparison["life_exp_1952"]
comparison.round(2)

Every continent saw double-digit growth in average life expectancy over this 55-year span. Asia recorded the largest absolute increase, adding over 24 years to its average.

Visualizing Regional Life Expectancy (2007)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
ax.bar(recent_summary['continent'], recent_summary['median_life_exp'], color='royalblue')
ax.set_title('Median Life Expectancy by Continent (2007)')
ax.set_ylabel('Median Life Expectancy (years)')
ax.set_xlabel('Continent')

# Add value labels on top of the bars for clarity
for i, v in enumerate(recent_summary['median_life_exp']):
    ax.text(i, v - 4, f"{v:.1f}", color='white', fontweight='bold', ha='center')

plt.show()








Key Findings:

Leading Regions: Oceania and Europe rank highest, with median life expectancies surpassing 80 and 76 years, respectively.
The Middle Tier: The Americas and Asia cluster in the low 70s, reflecting the rapid developmental strides in Asia that closed the historical gap with the Americas.
The Global Gap: Africa trails significantly with a median life expectancy of 52.9 years in 2007, a roughly 20-year deficit compared to the next lowest region.

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Creating Data in R
Data Source: The Gapminder dataset
License: Free to use under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
We will load a small sample natively in R to pass into Python.

library(gapminder)

# Grab the first 5 rows of the dataset (Afghanistan 1952-1972)
r_data <- head(gapminder, 5)
print(r_data)

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Reading R Data into Python
Accessing the R environment via the r. object in Python. A new column calculating life expectancy in months is appended to the dataframe using pandas.

import pandas as pd

python_df = r.r_data
python_df['lifeExp_months'] = python_df['lifeExp'] * 12

print(python_df)

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
section: Returning Python Data back to R
text:
Returning Python Data back to R
Retrieving the transformed object from the Python environment back into R using the py$ object.

final_r_data <- py$python_df

print(final_r_data)

2 Afghanistan      Asia 1957  30.332  9240934  820.8530        363.984
3 Afghanistan      Asia 1962  31.997 10267083  853.1007        383.964

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Visualizing the Round-Trip Data
To confirm the data remains fully functional for analysis after passing between languages, we can plot the newly calculated lifeExp_months column back in R.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(final_r_data, aes(x = factor(year), y = lifeExp_months)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Afghanistan Life Expectancy (1952-1972)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Life Expectancy (Months)"
  )








Interoperability Highlights:

Seamless Translation: The reticulate package automatically converts R data.frame objects into Python pandas DataFrames.
State Retention: Variables and dataframe columns modified in the Python environment are preserved and instantly accessible when returning to the R workspace.
